assessment: This article proposes a combination of biomechanical modeling and in-silico experiments, on a newly-curated passive-movement dataset, to elucidate the nature of computations in the proprioceptive pathway. The authors find that, in addition to its canonical role in representing the body state, the proprioceptive pathway may have evolved to recognize actions. Overall, the authors' findings lead to new hypotheses about proprioception that future in-vivo experiments could test.
